# SK0001 — The file is not formatted

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala format` would change this file.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.6 |

## Why

The formatting half of Skala and the analysis half are one report. A finding that says "this file is not formatted" carries the formatter's own edits as its fix, so a machine reading the SARIF can apply them without a second tool invocation and a human sees formatting and analysis in one list. It is a suggestion rather than a warning because formatting is unconditional and free: the gate that cares is `formatting: clean`, not a severity.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if(x){DoThing();}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (x) {
    DoThing();
}
```

## When it does not fire

None by construction: the finding is produced by running the formatter, so it exists exactly when the formatter has an edit to make. A file that does not parse produces SK9010 instead and is never reported here.

## Configuration

- `Every resharper_* formatting key; the finding is whatever the configured formatter does.`
